title: Crew Compass + Ops Muscle — October All-Hands
summary: Quarterly all-hands focused on operational readiness, hiring cadence, product launch timeline adjustments, and risk mitigation for Q4. Leadership gave a short roadmap update and prioritized three cross-functional plays: capacity stabilization, cost-signal improvements, and an incident response drill schedule.
action_items: Priya: Publish trimmed launch plan and ship checklist (due 2025-10-28)
Liam: Schedule two infra runbooks + drill dates (due 2025-11-05)
Maya: Start recruiter blitz and update hiring priorities doc (due 2025-10-24)
next_steps: Leadership to share condensed deck & playbook link
People ops to begin candidate prioritization this week
SRE to run a full P0 tabletop before Dec
transcript:
00:00:02 Elena: Hey everyone thanks for joining, happy Tuesday, we're gonna kick off — sorry, push a little bit to 10 — but we'll run right through. Um, short agenda: signals, hiring, launches, and a quick Q/A.
00:00:18 Audience: applause / background chatter
00:00:35 Derrick: Quick ops note first — we've seen the median p99 tail creep up over the last three weeks, mostly in europe region during spikes. I think it's an interplay of batching and our new kernel path. We've rolled a hotfix last night but it's still stabilizing.
00:00:58 Priya: To clarify, is that the new quantized route or the fallback?
00:01:05 Derrick: It's the quantized route; when sequence lengths spike it triggers fallback into the older kernels and the switching is where we saw overhead. The fix reduces the switch penalty by about 25% but we still need more telemetry.
00:01:28 Elena: Ok great, so quick ask — can the infra team make a short runbook so product PMs know when to flip to dedicated capacity? We don't want customers impacted.
00:01:42 Liam: Yeah I've got a draft, will circulate by EOD. We'll include a little flow chart: signal → burst → spin-up dedicated → graceful degradation.
00:01:57 Audience (murmur): mm-hmm
00:02:10 Maya: On hiring — we're hitting Q4 hiring targets slower than forecast. Time-to-offer sits at 42 days, target is 28. We agreed to a recruiter blitz, and I'm reprioritizing reqs to focus on infra and SRE first.
00:02:30 Elena: Is there anything blockers-wise — background checks? comp bands?
00:02:35 Maya: Mostly comp + interview funnel friction. Also we need faster deconflict for interviewers; calendar availability is killing us.
00:02:48 Priya: Would it help if we reduce stage count for infra roles to two technical interviews plus a leadership bar?
00:02:55 Maya: Yes, that's in the plan.
00:03:10 Derrick: A quick product update — the hosted API streaming change is in canary and we saw a 12% token cost reduction in the internal bench. It's not yet customer-safe for full rollout, there are some edge cases with function calling that need more tests.
00:03:36 Audience: hmm
00:03:45 Priya: We're trimming the initial launch surface for Oct to a single model family to simplify QA. We're postponing some peripheral features (structured output extras) to the November patch.
00:03:58 Elena: I want to emphasize simplicity over feature breadth for this launch; less to go wrong.
00:04:10 Nadia: On the customer side, renewals team is asking for more measurable latency guarantees in the deck. Can we provide p50/p95/p99 baked into the offering?
00:04:22 Derrick: We can provide profiles per model but I want to avoid hard SLAs for hosted until we finish some of the capacity work. For Dedicated we can be concrete.
00:04:37 Elena: So messaging — offer measured numbers for hosted as 'typical observed' and reserve SLA language for Dedicated. Please sync with marketing on phrasing.
00:04:53 Priya: We'll get the templated table to marketing by Friday.
00:05:10 Audience Q: (someone) What about private deployments and compliance timelines?
00:05:16 Elena: Good question — Private is slower because of custom network work. We're targeting two pilot customers by end of Q1. We're tracking the on-prem packaging and KMS integration as highest priority.
00:05:34 Liam: There's also a dependency on our installer — the version we tested had a kube networking quirk; operations are fixing that now.
00:05:47 Elena: Okay, pivot to risk: we had an incident simulation last week that surfaced a communications gap when the fallback policy kicks in.
00:05:58 Derrick: Right — the hardware fallback caused some routes to mislabel and our alerts weren't firing because the signal was treated as a normal diff. We'll change the alert thresholds and add an auto-tag so paging rules pick it up.
00:06:16 Audience: mm
00:06:30 Elena: I'm instituting a mandatory incident drill once per quarter. Liam will run the first one and report outcomes at the next all-hands.
00:06:40 Liam: Yep, scheduling for Nov 14 — full P0 tabletop.
00:06:48 Priya: Quick note on experiments — Redwood Optimize's new recommendations flow reduced token spend by 8% in a test run when we enabled prefix caching heuristics. We should consider an opt-in for power users.
00:07:05 Elena: Cool, but let's ensure it's behind a setting and clearly documented; we don't want surprises.
00:07:20 Audience laughter / light banter
00:07:35 Audience Q: Are we hiring in EMEA as aggressively?
00:07:40 Maya: Yes, but comp bands differ; we'll publish localized bands this week.
00:07:50 Audience: applause
00:08:02 Derrick: Security quick hit — SOC2 readiness progress is steady. The external assessor had a few minor findings around access reviews; we need to tighten RBAC audits.
00:08:20 Elena: Action — security to share the remediation tracker and timelines.
00:08:28 Priya: On metrics — finance will publish the unit economics dashboard next week; want everyone to see the cost-per-token trends and the areas where caching helped. This will drive the Optimize play prioritization.
00:08:48 Audience: chatter
00:09:05 Elena: Ok let's go through a lightning round from each leader — Derrick, one minute on infra; Priya one minute on product; Maya one minute on people; Liam one minute on ops.
00:09:18 Derrick: Infra — we're focusing on the kernel selector and telemetry, adding a lightweight 'mode' that favors latency over cost for labeled routes. Expect a config flag in two sprints.
00:09:35 Priya: Product — trimmed launch, focusing on 'predictable experience' for the first customers, shipping core streaming + function call stability.
00:09:46 Maya: People — recruiter blitz, fewer interview stages for infra, internal referral push and an updated hiring priorities doc.
00:09:58 Liam: Ops — runbooks, auto-tagging for alerts, SRE rotations to include a 'guardrail' pager for degradation scenarios.
00:10:10 Audience applause
00:10:30 Audience Q: (someone) What's the budget ask for Q4 hiring?
00:10:35 Elena: We reprioritized spend — a small bump reserved for critical hires, we'll share exact numbers with finance next week.
00:10:46 Priya: There's also a small runway risk if the hosting cost per token doesn't trend down, which is why Optimize is important.
00:10:58 Audience: mm-hmm
00:11:15 Nadia: From customer success — please make sure the launch notes include an escalation path and who to contact for warm handoffs.
00:11:24 Priya: We'll add a one-page runbook for onboarding customers during launch.
00:11:34 Audience: chatter
00:11:50 Audience Question: (someone off mic) Will there be a public post about this roadmap?
00:11:56 Elena: Yes, a short blog post after launch and a more technical notes doc for customers.
00:12:08 Audience: applause
00:12:20 Priya: Ok quick housekeeping — next all-hands will be early Jan to do a full quarter review and goals reset.
00:12:30 Maya: Also internal offsite planning is in progress — calendar invites to follow.
00:12:38 Audience: light laughter
00:12:55 Elena: Closing — appreciate the focus, let's keep the communication tight. I'll hand it to Q/A for a few minutes.
00:13:08 Audience Q: (someone) Can we get more granular p99 numbers by model family?
00:13:14 Derrick: We'll publish a profiles table but remember it's representative and varies with seq len and workload.
00:13:25 Audience Q: (someone) Any changes to our evaluation benchmarks?
00:13:30 Priya: We're standardizing on a smaller prompt suite for the initial launch to speed the QA loop.
00:13:42 Audience Q: (someone) Are we pausing any feature work?
00:13:46 Elena: Yes a few low-impact features are deferred to Nov.
00:13:55 Audience: wrap-up chatter
00:14:10 Elena: Thanks all, we'll post the notes and the deck.
00:14:18 Meeting ends (camera off)

Note: Transcript sampling stopped at 14 minutes for brevity; full meeting recording exists in drive link: https://redwood.internal/allhands/2025-10-21-crew-compass and deck: https://redwood.internal/decks/crew-compass-oct2025.pdf
